comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
DIRECTION FROM OPERATOR: do not pin a local update tool. Recording the consequences, and a correction to my own earlier recommendation.

MY RECOMMENDATION WAS WRONG ON THE FACTS. I proposed 'brew upgrade uv' as the minimal unblock. That cannot work: required-version is '==0.12.7', an EXACT pin, and Homebrew has moved PAST it to 0.12.9 (2026-09-01). Verified empirically against a scratch pyproject carrying the same pin:
  /opt/homebrew/bin/uv 0.12.9  -> error: Required uv version `==0.12.7` does not match the running version `0.12.9`
  ~/.local/bin/uv     0.12.7  -> Resolved 1 package
Upgrading Homebrew only changes which number appears in the error. The scheduled 00:32 run confirms it independently: it failed with 0.12.9 and pushed the streak to 120. I should have checked the pin's comparison operator before recommending an upgrade.

THIS IS THE FEBD FAILURE, VERSION FOR VERSION. scripts/check_uv_pin.py's docstring describes the outage as: 'every build died with Required uv version ==0.12.7 does not match the running version 0.12.9 the moment :latest moved -- a time bomb armed by an upstream release, with no change to this repository.' The version in that sentence is 0.12.9, which is what Homebrew now ships. So this host's updater is the SAME time bomb with a different fuse: not a floating Docker tag, but a package manager that upgraded past the pin. Four consumers of one exact pin, three of which were never brought along.

RELAXING THE PIN IS NOT AVAILABLE. check_uv_pin.py deliberately fails the build when the pin is 'loosened to a range' (its point 2) or overridden per call site (point 3), because an exact pin is the property under test. So the fix cannot be a wider constraint in pyproject.toml.

WHAT THE DIRECTION MEANS FOR AC2. The updater is a local dev-tracking tool, not CI; it gains no reproducibility from being locked to any particular uv binary, and the current hardcode (UV_BIN default /opt/homebrew/bin/uv at rebar-dev-update.sh:18) is itself a local pin -- the one that broke. So AC2 stands as written and should be read as explicitly EXCLUDING a new hardcoded path: the updater must DERIVE the uv it needs from the CANDIDATE COMMIT's own required-version at sync time, since that value changes as main moves, and fail loudly naming required version, found version, and paths inspected when none satisfies it. Substituting one absolute path for another (either direction) is rejected -- it re-inverts the moment the other side updates first, which is exactly how this stall was born.

AC3 RESCOPED per operator decision: do NOT pursue the cross-account SNS authorization. The alert sink stays as-is. AC4 (a LOCAL detector that surfaces a stalled updater or an over-stale build without depending on the remote sink) absorbs the detection requirement and is the priority half -- it is the thing that would actually have caught 120 silent failures.

IMMEDIATE STATE: no persistent host change made. No plist edit, no REBAR_DEV_UV_BIN pin. Homebrew's uv did move 0.12.6 -> 0.12.9 during investigation (a relink surfaced by 'brew upgrade'; both versions fail the pin identically, so no behavior changed). The global rebar remains at cdfd7d94d and stale until AC2 lands or an operator runs a one-shot.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
AC4 (local detector) IMPLEMENTED and independently verified on this host. AC2 patch written but NOT applied -- awaiting operator decision, since the target is a machine-local script.

THE DETECTOR REPORTS THE REAL BUG. Verified by me directly, not taken on report:
  doctor: build freshness
    [error] reject-streak: the main-tracking updater has rejected 122 consecutive candidates (threshold 3) ...
    [error] build-stale: the published rebar build (cdfd7d94d, 2026-08-29) is 201 commit(s) behind origin/main (6125c5345), over the 25-commit threshold -- gate results from it can be wrong in ways the verdict cannot show
Note the numbers MOVED between the implementer's run and mine: streak 121 -> 122, drift 200 -> 201. The stall is ongoing and worsening hourly, which is itself corroboration.

SHAPE: a scan module inside the existing 'rebar doctor' command, NOT a new scripts/check_*.py. The check_orphaned_load.py precedent was weighed and SPLIT rather than copied: its ON-DEMAND half is exactly right (live host state is not a property of the tree under review, so it does not belong in make lint), but its LOCATION is not -- scripts/ is where this repo puts things that gate or report on the TREE. doctor_mcp_client.py is the closer structural match: it reads the operator's home directory, degrades every fault to a finding, renders its own section, and stays advisory outside the exit code and outside --repair. That contract was copied exactly, plus a has_blocking_build_freshness() seam for a caller that does want to gate. AC4 also names a 'rebar' invocation as its first example. Secondary argument, and a good one: an operator already runs 'rebar doctor', whereas a script nobody knows exists is a detector with the same silence problem as the dead SNS topic.

TWO INDEPENDENT SIGNALS, deliberately not one: reject-streak catches an updater that is FAILING; build-stale (>25 commits behind) catches one that STOPPED RUNNING, and survives a hand-reset counter. Threshold justified from data rather than picked: a healthy hourly updater sits 0-2 commits behind, and the two recorded incidents were ~48 and ~195, so 25 is below the smaller incident and an order of magnitude above healthy.

REUSE, NOT REIMPLEMENTATION: the commit-distance walk is build_drift.detect_drift, extended with one keyword-only build_sha parameter defaulting to running_build_sha(). It previously read only the RUNNING process's sha, which cannot answer 'how stale is the build the updater published' from a dev checkout. All existing callers unchanged.

NO NEW MECHANISM. _detect_gate_scripts was checked BEFORE designing (it names a ci_gate by the repo-relative path of any scripts/check_*.py), which is precisely why the detector is not one. check_mechanism_delta.py --check reports new=0, and test_mechanism_delta.py passes 31/31. No marker, no baseline edit.

A GATE CAUGHT A DESIGN FICTION, worth recording as a positive: the first draft read XDG_STATE_HOME, which check_config_ownership.py rejected as an 'unresolved-env-read below approved seam'. Rather than add a marker to keep it, the env read was REMOVED -- because the updater itself does not consult XDG_STATE_HOME (its default is ${HOME}/.local/state/rebar-dev), so honoring it described a layout that is never written. The module now reads no environment at all. The gate did not just block a violation; it surfaced that the code was accommodating something fictional. Documented limitation: an operator who relocated state via the updater's own REBAR_DEV_STATE_DIR passes state_dir= to the scan.

Verification: make lint exit 0; make typecheck clean (755 files); test_mechanism_delta.py 31 passed; 110 targeted passed; 102 regression passed. RED first: ImportError for the absent module, then 14 passed.

AC2 PATCH READY BUT UNAPPLIED. Live ~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh confirmed byte-identical to its original. It honors the operator's direction -- no pinned local tool, and no substituted absolute path: UV_BIN's hardcoded default is removed, REBAR_DEV_UV_BIN survives only as a HINT that is validated like any other candidate rather than trusted, and the pin is read from the CANDIDATE COMMIT's own pyproject.toml AFTER checkout (the earliest point it exists, and why the value tracks main rather than this host). Every uv on PATH is probed by --version and the first exact match wins, so PATH ORDER STOPS BEING LOAD-BEARING in either direction. Exact string comparison suffices without a version solver because check_uv_pin.py contractually guarantees an exact ==X.Y.Z and fails the build on a range; any other shape is refused loudly rather than guessed.

Exercised against the real host (functions extracted to a harness; the updater itself never run):
  real pyproject ==0.12.7  -> selects ~/.local/bin/uv, THE BINARY THE CURRENT HARDCODE EXCLUDES
  unsatisfiable ==9.9.9    -> names required version, every version found, and every path inspected
  wrong hint (0.12.9)      -> rejected, correct 0.12.7 chosen (validated, not trusted)
  range pin / no pin       -> refused loudly
Failures now reject at a new 'uv-select' stage, so the log and reject-streak name binary selection rather than blaming sync.

AC1 depends on AC2 being applied (operator's call). AC3 was rescoped away by the operator. AC5 (pruner 'Directory not empty' and the 5fb69334...1559 partial-release stub) remains open and untouched.

AC2 HAS NO REPO-SIDE TEST and cannot have one: the script is machine-local and git-ignored, so nothing in the tree can reach it. The evidence is the harness run above.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
INCIDENT DETAIL MOVED OUT OF THE DESCRIPTION (nothing deleted — preserved here verbatim in substance).

Reason for the move: `review-plan` BLOCKED the ticket on two deterministic criteria (P1 readiness-shape: no `## Acceptance Criteria` heading with `- [ ]` items; P10 verification-presence: no `## Testing` section and no AC naming a proving command), and the description was at 7,556 of the 8,000-character admission cap (P4) — only 444 characters of headroom. Adding the required structure was impossible without first moving narrative into a comment. The description now carries the plan and its acceptance criteria; the forensic detail lives here.

## Root cause, in full

`~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh:18` hardcodes the uv binary:

    UV_BIN="${REBAR_DEV_UV_BIN:-/opt/homebrew/bin/uv}"

and `:120` orders PATH to keep it authoritative, reasoning at `:116-118`:

    # launchd gives a minimal PATH. Keep Homebrew before ~/.local/bin so the obsolete
    # standalone uv there cannot shadow the pinned UV_BIN.
    export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:${HOME}/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"

Measured on this host: `/opt/homebrew/bin/uv` is 0.12.9 (Homebrew moved 0.12.6 -> 0.12.9 during investigation); `/Users/joeoakhart/.local/bin/uv` is 0.12.7 (standalone, 2026-08-27). `pyproject.toml` pins `required-version = "==0.12.7"` (commit 7501cc1d602d). uv reads `required-version` itself and fails fast, so `:344`'s `"$UV_BIN" sync` aborts every run.

THE COMMENT'S PREMISE INVERTED. When written, `~/.local/bin` held the obsolete uv, so pinning to Homebrew was right. Homebrew is now the stale side. The guard written to stop a stale uv being selected became the mechanism selecting one. Hardcoding EITHER absolute path re-inverts the next time one side updates first — which is why AC2 requires derivation, not substitution.

## This is the febd failure, version for version

`scripts/check_uv_pin.py`'s docstring describes that outage: "every build died with `Required uv version ==0.12.7 does not match the running version 0.12.9` the moment `:latest` moved — a time bomb armed by an upstream release, with no change to this repository." The version in that sentence, 0.12.9, is what Homebrew now ships. Same exact pin, same version, different fuse: a package manager that upgraded past the pin rather than a floating Docker tag. Four consumers of one pin; three were never brought along.

RELAXING THE PIN IS NOT AVAILABLE: `check_uv_pin.py` fails the build when the pin is loosened to a range (its point 2) or overridden per call site (point 3). An exact pin is the property under test.

## The alert that should have caught this

`REJECT_STREAK_ALERT` (default 3) was added after "the b477339a99 incident: 43 hourly `sync` rejections, ~48 commits behind, no signal". It fired correctly and failed to deliver every time:

    aws: [ERROR]: An error occurred (AuthorizationError) when calling the Publish operation:
    User: arn:aws:iam::820258254566:user/joeoakhart is not authorized to perform: SNS:Publish
    on resource: arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:896586841071:rebar-gerrit-alerts

IAM principal in account 820258254566; topic in 896586841071; no resource-based policy permits the cross-account publish. The streak reached 120+ against a threshold of 3 with zero operator signal.

## Impact

Every agent session on this host invoking the global `rebar` ran a build ~195 commits stale for about five days. The gate's own advisory: "this rebar build (cdfd7d94d, 2026-08-29, dirty) is 195 commit(s) BEHIND the ref this gate pinned (08a39c39c) — it may predate recent config keys and gate fixes, so results can be wrong in ways the verdict cannot show." That reaches plan-review and completion-verifier verdicts produced through the global tool. Noticed only because a subagent's gate log was read closely.

## Secondary defect (AC5)

`launchd.err.log` shows the pruner failing to reclaim release dirs:

    rm: .../releases/5b5008bbfbec...66068/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages: Directory not empty
    rm: .../releases/5fb693345b0c...1559: Directory not empty

`releases/5fb693345b0cd1b48d1e9d20b292fd15761c7624.1559` is a 3-entry stub — a partially built release never completed or cleaned. Related to the disk-ceiling work under epic 6202-e1c7-c57f-4897; these dirs are ~346 MB each.

## Ongoing

The stall is live and worsening: reject-streak 121 -> 122 and drift 200 -> 201 commits were observed within a single working session.

comments.body:
AC4 pushed for review: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2608 (commit f50dc1007bd0, Change-Id I55bc93a0a81b4dcd011c733b02e6d9dac3a9cf34).

SCOPE OF THIS CHANGE: AC4 ONLY. rebar doctor gains a build-freshness section reading two independent local signals -- reject-streak (the updater's own counter vs its threshold of 3) and build-stale (the build behind the current pointer more than 25 commits behind origin/main). No network, no credential, no CI provider. Advisory: printed in text and JSON, outside doctor's exit code and outside --repair, on the same grounds doctor already applies to HOME-sourced MCP-client findings. Absent updater state emits one 'unavailable' finding, never a failure.

Files: src/rebar/_commands/doctor_build_freshness.py (new), src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py (wiring), src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py (optional build_sha so the EXISTING ancestry walk can measure a build this process is not executing -- reuse, not a second walk), tests/unit/test_doctor_build_freshness.py (new, RED-first), docs/user-guide.md.

NO NEW MECHANISM. A scripts/check_*.py would have registered a ci_gate named by its path (scripts/_mechanism_delta/detect_ci.py::_detect_gate_scripts), which --check admits via a marker but tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py rejects regardless (the contradiction filed as a1f1-a30d-2d50-4f5a). Delivering this inside the existing rebar doctor command avoids the kind entirely: check_mechanism_delta.py --check reports new=0 increased=0 stale=0 and test_mechanism_delta.py passes 31/31. No marker added, no baseline edited.

An XDG_STATE_HOME read was REMOVED rather than marked: check_config_ownership.py flagged it as an unresolved-env-read below an approved seam, and the updater does not consult that variable anyway, so the code was accommodating a layout that is never written. The module now reads no environment at all.

GATES: review-plan PASS and SIGNED at head_sha f50dc1007bd0 (verified_at_sha 6125c5345f01). Three runs: run 1 blocked deterministically in 6s with no LLM spend (P1 readiness-shape, P10 verification-presence); run 2 blocked on one LLM finding (AC4 named no staleness threshold); run 3 passed. The description was rewritten to the standard checklist shape and the incident forensics moved to the preceding comment -- it was at 7,556 of the 8,000-char admission cap with 444 chars of headroom, so the required structure could not be added without moving narrative out. file_impact recorded across the 5 files.

Verification: make lint exit 0 (ruff, complexity new=0 increased=0, mechanism new=0, config-ownership, uv-pin, zizmor, actionlint); make typecheck clean over 755 files; 110 targeted tests + 102 regression tests pass. On this host the detector reports the live bug: reject-streak 122, build-stale 201 commits, both climbing hourly.

STILL OPEN: AC1 and AC2 (with the operator as an unapplied diff to the machine-local, git-ignored rebar-dev-update.sh -- outside any repository test's reach) and AC5 (pruner Directory-not-empty + the 5fb69334...1559 stub). AC3 withdrawn by operator decision. NOT closing this ticket.

Carried advisory from run 3, recorded rather than actioned: build_drift.detect_drift performs no fetch, so origin/main is whatever the local checkout last fetched -- a checkout that has not fetched recently UNDERSTATES drift. That is the conservative direction (it never invents drift) and is documented at the TRACKED_REF constant, but a future change could resolve the ref via a bounded best-effort git ls-remote degrading to unavailable.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
AC1 SATISFIED -- THE STALL IS OVER. AC2 patch applied to ~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh with operator approval, original backed up to rebar-dev-update.sh.pre-ac97.bak, and the updater run once to verify on the real thing rather than a harness.

Result:
  2026-09-04T05:06:47Z updated -> 6125c5345f0117d377acf72975c7c547316e537a (locked runtime; click override from uv.lock)
  2026-09-04T05:06:46Z prune summary: pruned=2 kept-live=0 remaining=4 (keep=3 cap=10)
  reject-streak: 122 -> 0
  current: releases/cdfd7d94d... (2026-08-28) -> releases/6125c5345f01... (current main)

So 122 consecutive failures and 201 commits of drift are ended, and the run also reclaimed two stale
release directories on its way through. Every session on this host now gets gate verdicts from
current code rather than a five-day-old build; the on-box MCP server is likewise no longer serving
stale gate code.

APPLICATION NOTE for whoever repeats this: 'git apply' REFUSES the diff because it names orig.sh /
new.sh -- it was generated from an extraction harness, not from a checkout. Use patch(1) against the
target explicitly: patch ~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh < <diff>. It applied cleanly, bash -n is
clean, and the hardcode at :18 is now UV_BIN="" with selection at :190.

WHY THIS FIX SHOULD NOT RE-INVERT, restated now that it is live: no absolute path is baked in.
PATH ORDER IS NO LONGER LOAD-BEARING -- every uv on PATH is probed by --version and the first exact
match wins, so neither Homebrew nor ~/.local/bin can shadow a satisfying binary in either direction.
The pin is read from the CANDIDATE COMMIT's own pyproject.toml after checkout, so it tracks main
rather than this host, which is the property the old hardcode lacked. REBAR_DEV_UV_BIN survives only
as a hint that is validated like any other candidate, never trusted.

STILL OPEN ON THIS TICKET:
 - AC4's detector is pushed for review as Gerrit change 2608 (not yet voted). Note it will now report
   CLEAN on this host, which is correct -- its live-host reading was already demoted to a one-time
   recorded datum (122 / 201 on 2026-09-03) precisely because AC1 destroys the observable condition.
   That AC-ordering fix has now paid off in practice rather than in theory.
 - AC5 (pruner 'Directory not empty' failures, and the 5fb693345b0c...1559 partial-release stub)
   remains open and untouched. Today's run pruned two releases successfully, so it is worth
   re-checking whether AC5 still reproduces before scoping work for it.
 - AC3 stays withdrawn per operator decision; AC4 absorbs its detection requirement.

compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

The hourly LaunchAgent `com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`, which keeps this host's **global**
`rebar` / `rebar-mcp` aligned to `origin/main`, has failed 120+ consecutive times and is
still failing. The global build is pinned at `cdfd7d94dc2fe7671a7eba48e31f36c30f39235c`
(2026-08-28) — 201 commits behind `origin/main` at the latest check, and climbing hourly.
`launchctl list` reports last exit status 1 for the agent.

Every hourly run logs the same rejection:

```
error: Required uv version `==0.12.7` does not match the running version `0.12.9`
candidate ebbcd7a030d6... rejected at sync; current left untouched
candidate-rejection streak now 122 (latest stage: sync)
```

## Root cause

`~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh:18` hardcodes `UV_BIN` to an absolute Homebrew path and
`:120` orders PATH to keep it authoritative. That premise has INVERTED: Homebrew's uv is now
0.12.9, past the repository's exact `required-version = "==0.12.7"`, while the
`~/.local/bin` standalone sits at 0.12.7. The guard written to stop a stale uv being
selected is now the mechanism selecting one. Substituting the other absolute path
re-inverts the moment that side updates first. Full forensics — the `febd` precedent, the
SNS failure, and the impact measurement — are preserved in the ticket comments.

## The detection gap is the priority half

`REJECT_STREAK_ALERT` (threshold 3) fired every hour and failed to deliver every time: the
IAM principal is in account 820258254566, the SNS topic in 896586841071, and no
resource-based policy permits the cross-account publish. The streak therefore reached 120+
against a threshold of 3 with zero operator signal. Whatever causes the next stall, it is
equally silent unless a detector exists that does not depend on a remote sink.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — An on-demand `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`
  publishes a `current` whose sha equals `origin/main` at that moment. Checked by
  `[ "$(cat ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/current/sha)" = "$(git ls-remote origin main | cut -f1)" ]`,
  by `! grep -q '^error: Required uv version' ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/update.log`, and by
  `[ "$(cat ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/reject-streak)" -eq 0 ]`.
- [ ] AC2 — The updater selects a uv satisfying the CANDIDATE COMMIT's own
  `required-version`, read from that commit's `pyproject.toml` at sync time, rather than any
  hardcoded absolute path. When no available uv satisfies it, the run fails with a message
  naming the required version, each version found, and each path inspected. DISPOSITION of
  that failure is a SOFT RETRY, not a terminal stop: the candidate is rejected at its own
  `uv-select` stage, `current` is left untouched, the streak increments, and the next hourly
  tick retries — matching the existing `rejected at sync; current left untouched` behaviour,
  so a since-fixed or transient pin heals without operator action. Checked by running the
  resolver against a checkout whose pin no local uv satisfies and asserting the message
  names all three facts, and against one whose pin is satisfiable and asserting it selects
  that uv.
- [ ] AC3 — WITHDRAWN by operator decision: the cross-account SNS authorization is not
  being pursued and the sink stays as-is. AC4 absorbs the detection requirement.
- [ ] AC4 — A stalled updater or an over-stale build is detectable locally, with no
  dependency on the alert path, via two INDEPENDENT signals in `rebar doctor`:
  `reject-streak` (the updater's own counter at or above its alert threshold, default 3,
  mirroring the updater's own `REJECT_STREAK_ALERT`) and `build-stale` (the build behind the
  updater's `current` pointer more than **25 commits** behind `origin/main`). Both
  thresholds are named module constants carrying those defaults, overridable per call
  through the scan's `reject_streak_alert` / `max_commits_behind` parameters; they are
  deliberately NOT config keys or env vars, because the mechanism-delta ratchet counts those
  and this needs no new configuration surface. 25 is chosen because an hourly updater sits
  at 0-2 commits behind when healthy, while the two recorded incidents reached ~48 and ~195,
  so it falls below the smaller incident and an order of magnitude above healthy. ABSENT
  STATE IS NOT A FAILURE: on a box running no such updater the scan emits exactly one
  `unavailable` finding and nothing else, and every finding is ADVISORY — printed in text
  and JSON, kept out of `doctor`'s exit code and out of `--repair`, on the same grounds
  `doctor` already applies to HOME-sourced MCP-client findings. Checked by
  `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_doctor_build_freshness.py -q`, which drives BOTH signals
  and the absent-state path against a synthetic state directory and a throwaway git repo.
  That proof is deliberately independent of live host state, because AC1 REMOVES the
  condition being detected: once AC1 lands the host is neither stalled nor stale, so a check
  worded as "observe it on this host" would become unrunnable the moment AC1 succeeded. The
  live-host observation is instead recorded once, as evidence the detector fires on the real
  incident: on 2026-09-03 `rebar doctor` reported reject-streak 122 and build-stale 201.
- [ ] AC5 — The pruner's `Directory not empty` failures are resolved and the partial
  release stub `5fb693345b0cd...1559` is reclaimed. Checked by
  `! ls ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/releases | grep -q '^5fb693345b0cd'`, and by
  `! grep -q 'Directory not empty' ~/.local/state/rebar-dev/launchd.err.log` after a
  subsequent run.

## Testing

Repository-side (AC4), from a worktree with `.venv/bin` first on `PATH`:

```
python -m pytest tests/unit/test_doctor_build_freshness.py -q
python -m pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py -q
make lint
make typecheck
```

`test_doctor_build_freshness.py` is the named coverage for BOTH AC4 signals, not only
`build-stale`: it asserts the `reject-streak` finding at, above and below its threshold and
on a corrupt counter; the `build-stale` finding above and below its threshold and on a sha
absent from the repo; the absent-state `unavailable` path; and that both reach an operator
through `rebar doctor` in text and JSON without altering its exit code.

Host-side (AC1, AC2, AC5) cannot be covered by a repository test: `rebar-dev-update.sh` is
machine-local and git-ignored, so it lies outside any test's reach. Those are proven by the
observations named in their acceptance criteria, run against the live updater, and the
AC2 resolver is exercised against a harness carrying the real pin.

## Constraints

- Do not pin a local update tool. The required uv version moves as `main` moves, so it must
  be read per candidate commit rather than baked into this host.
- The pin cannot be widened: `check_uv_pin.py` fails the build when `required-version` is
  loosened to a range or overridden per call site, because an exact pin is the property
  under test.

AC4: wire the build-freshness scan into doctor as its own advisory section (text + JSON)
AC4: add an optional build_sha so the existing ancestry walk can measure a build this process is not executing
AC4: RED-first tests for both signals, the not-applicable path, and the doctor wiring
AC4: document the build-freshness section and why the detector is local
